devdoc.author: Angle Core Team
devdoc.details: There is one `PerpetualManager` contract per pair stablecoin/collateral in the protocolThis file contains the functions of the `PerpetualManager` that can be directly interacted with by external agents. These functions are the ones that need to be called to open, modify or close perpetuals`PerpetualManager` naturally handles staking, the code allowing HAs to stake has been inspired from https://github.com/SetProtocol/index-coop-contracts/blob/master/contracts/staking/StakingRewardsV2.solPerpetuals at Angle protocol are treated as NFTs, this contract handles the logic for that

addToPerpetual(uint256,uint256).details: This decreases the leverage multiple of this perpetualIf this perpetual is to be liquidated, the HA is not going to be able to add liquidity to itSince this function can be used to add liquidity to a perpetual, there is no need to restrict it to the owner of the perpetualCalling this function on a non-existing perpetual makes it revert

params.amount: Amount to add to the perpetual's `margin`
params.perpetualID: ID of the perpetual to which amount should be added to `margin`

approve(address,uint256).details: The approved address will have the right to transfer the perpetual, to cash it out on behalf of the owner, to add or remove collateral in it and to choose the destination address that will be able to receive the proceeds of the perpetual

params.to: Address to approve the perpetual to

balanceOf(address).details: Balance here represents the number of perpetuals owned by a HA

closePerpetual(uint256,address,uint256).details: The HA gets the current amount of her position depending on the entry oracle value and current oracle value minus some transaction fees computed on the committed amount`msg.sender` should be the owner of `perpetualID` or be approved for this perpetualIf the `PoolManager` does not have enough collateral, the perpetual owner will be converted to a SLP and receive sanTokensThe `minCashOutAmount` serves as a protection for HAs closing their perpetuals: it protects them both from fees that would have become too high and from a too big decrease in oracle value

params.minCashOutAmount: Minimum net cash out amount that the HA is willing to get for closing the perpetual
params.perpetualID: ID of the perpetual to close
params.to: Address which will receive the proceeds from this perpetual

deployCollateral(address[],address,addre.details: Called by the `PoolManager` contract when it is activated by the `StableMaster`The `governorList` and `guardian` here are those of the `Core` contract

params.feeManager_: Reference to the `FeeManager` contract which will be able to update fees
params.governorList: List of governor addresses of the protocol
params.guardian: Address of the guardian of the protocol
params.oracle_: Reference to the `oracle` contract which will be able to update fees

params.perpetualID: ID of the perpetual to check

forceClosePerpetuals(uint256[]).details: This function allows to make sure that the protocol will not have too much HAs for a long period of timeA HA that owns a targeted perpetual will get the current value of her perpetualThe call to the function above will revert if HAs cannot be cashed outAs keepers may directly profit from this function, there may be front-running problems with miners bots, we may have to put an access control logic for this function to only allow white-listed addresses to act as keepers for the protocol

getCashOutAmount(uint256,uint256).details: This function is used by the Collateral Settlement contract

returns._1: Whether the position of the perpetual is now too small compared with its initial position and should hence be liquidated

params.perpetualID: ID of the perpetual which accumulated tokens

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role.

initialize(address,address).details: The reward token is most likely going to be the ANGLE tokenSince this contract is upgradeable, this function is an `initialize` and not a `constructor`Zero checks are only performed on addresses for which no external calls are made, in this case just the `rewardToken_` is checkedAfter initializing this contract, all the fee parameters should be initialized by governance using the setters in this contract

params.poolManager_: Reference to the `PoolManager` contract handling the collateral associated to the `PerpetualManager`
params.rewardToken_: Reference to the `rewardtoken` that can be distributed to HAs as they have open positions

liquidatePerpetuals(uint256[]).details: Liquidation of a perpetual will succeed if the `cashOutAmount` of the perpetual is under the maintenance margin, and nothing will happen if the perpetual is still healthyThe outside caller (namely a keeper) gets a portion of the leftover cash out amount of the perpetualAs keepers may directly profit from this function, there may be front-running problems with miners bots, we may have to put an access control logic for this function to only allow white-listed addresses to act as keepers for the protocol

notifyRewardAmount(uint256).details: Only the reward distributor contract is allowed to call this function which starts a staking cycleThis function is the equivalent of the `notifyRewardAmount` function found in all staking contracts

params.reward: Amount of governance tokens to be distributed to HAs

openPerpetual(address,uint256,uint256,ui.details: The future owner of the perpetual cannot be the zero addressIt is possible to open a perpetual on behalf of someone elseThe `maxOracleRate` parameter serves as a protection against oracle manipulations for HAs opening perpetuals`minNetMargin` is a protection against too big variations in the fees for HAs

params.committedAmount: Amount of collateral covered by the HA
params.margin: Amount of collateral brought by the HA
params.maxOracleRate: Maximum oracle value that the HA wants to see stored in the perpetual
params.minNetMargin: Minimum net margin that the HA is willing to see stored in the perpetual
params.owner: Address of the future owner of the perpetual

returns.perpetualID: The ID of the perpetual opened by this HA

pause().details: After calling this function, it is going to be impossible for HAs to interact with their perpetuals or claim their rewards on it

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

params.tokenAddress: Address of the token to transfer

removeFromPerpetual(uint256,uint256,addr.details: This increases the leverage multiple of this perpetual`msg.sender` should be the owner of `perpetualID` or be approved for this perpetual

params.amount: Amount to remove from the perpetual's `margin`
params.perpetualID: ID of the perpetual from which collateral should be removed
params.to: Address which will receive the collateral removed from this perpetual

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `account`.

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role.

params.perpetualID: ID of the perpetual to transfer
ID of the perpetual to transfer

params.approved: Whether the sender wants to approve or block the operator
params.operator: Address to approve (or block) on all perpetuals

setBoundsPerpetual(uint64,uint64).details: For a perpetual, the leverage is defined as the ratio between the committed amount and the marginFor a perpetual, the maintenance margin is defined as the ratio between the margin ratio / the committed amount

params._maxLeverage: New value of the maximum leverage allowed

setFeeKeeper(uint64,uint64).details: Governance may decide to incorporate a collateral ratio dependence in the fees for HAs, in this case it will be done through the `FeeManager` contractThis dependence can either be a bonus or a malus

setFeeManager(address).details: This allows the `PoolManager` contract to propagate changes to the `PerpetualManager`This is the only place where the `_feeManager` can be changed, it is as if there was a `FEEMANAGER_ROLE` for which `PoolManager` was the admin

setHAFees(uint64[],uint64[],uint8).details: Evolution of the fees is linear between two values of thresholdsThese x values should be ranked in ascending orderFor deposit fees, the higher the x that is the ratio between what's to hedge and what's hedged the higher y should be (the more expensive it should be for HAs to come in)For withdraw fees, evolution should follow an opposite logic

params._xHAFees: Array of the x-axis value for the fees (deposit or withdraw)
params._yHAFees: Array of the y-axis value for the fees (deposit or withdraw)
params.deposit: Whether deposit or withdraw fees should be updated

params._keeperFeesClosingCap: Maximum reward going to the keeper forcing the closing of an ensemble of perpetuals
params._keeperFeesLiquidationCap: Maximum reward going to the keeper liquidating a perpetual

setKeeperFeesClosing(uint64[],uint64[]).details: The x thresholds correspond to values of the hedge ratio divided by two`xKeeperFeesClosing` and `yKeeperFeesClosing` should have the same length

params._yKeeperFeesClosing: Value of the fees at the different threshold values specified in `xKeeperFeesClosing`

setKeeperFeesLiquidationRatio(uint64).details: This proportion should be inferior to `BASE_PARAMS`

setLockTime(uint64).details: This parameter is used to prevent HAs from exiting before a certain amount of time and taking advantage of insiders' information they may have due to oracle latency

setNewRewardsDistribution(address).details: This function is part of the staking rewards interface and it is used to propagate a change of rewards distributor notified by the current `rewardsDistribution` addressIt has already been checked in the `RewardsDistributor` contract calling this function that the `newRewardsDistributor` had a compatible reward tokenWith this function, everything is as if `rewardsDistribution` was admin of its own role

params._rewardsDistribution: Address of the new rewards distributor contract

setOracle(address).details: The collateral `PoolManager` does not store a reference to an oracle, the value of the oracle is hence directly set by the `StableMaster`

setRewardDistribution(uint256,address).details: It allows governance to directly change the rewards distribution contract and the conditions at which this distribution is doneThe compatibility of the reward token is not checked here: it is checked in the rewards distribution contract when activating this as a staking contract, so if a reward distributor is set here but does not have a compatible reward token, then this reward distributor will not be able to set this contract as a staking contract

params._rewardsDistribution: Address which will give the reward tokens
params._rewardsDuration: Duration for the rewards for this contract

setTargetAndLimitHAHedge(uint64,uint64).details: `targetHAHedge` equal to `BASE_PARAMS` means that all the collateral from users should be insured by HAs`targetHAHedge` equal to 0 means HA should not cover (hedge) anything

params._limitHAHedge: Proportion of collateral from users above which HAs can see their perpetuals cashed out
params._targetHAHedge: Proportion of collateral from users that HAs should hedge

supportsInterface(bytes4).details: Interface identification is specified in ERC-165. This function uses less than 30,000 gas. Required by the ERC721 standard, so used to check that the IERC721 is implemented.

params.interfaceId: The interface identifier, as specified in ERC-165

returns._0: `true` if the contract implements `interfaceID` and  `interfaceID` is not 0xffffffff, `false` otherwise

params.perpetualID: ID of the perpetual to transfer

devdoc.title: PerpetualManagerFront

BASE_PARAMS().notice: Base that is used to define parameters that need to have a floating value (for instance parameters that are defined as ratios)

BASE_TOKENS().notice: Base that is used to compute ratios and floating numbers

GUARDIAN_ROLE().notice: Role for guardians, governors and `StableMaster` Made for the `StableMaster` to be able to update some parameters

addToPerpetual(uint256,uint256).notice: Lets a HA increase the `margin` in a perpetual she controls for this stablecoin/collateral pair

approve(address,uint256).notice: Approves to an address specified by `to` a perpetual specified by `perpetualID`

balanceOf(address).notice: Gets the balance of an owner

baseURI().notice: URI used for the metadata of the perpetuals

closePerpetual(uint256,address,uint256).notice: Lets a HA close a perpetual owned or controlled for the stablecoin/collateral pair associated to this `PerpetualManager` contract

deployCollateral(address[],address,addre.notice: Notifies the address of the `_feeManager` and of the `oracle` to this contract and grants the correct roles

earned(uint256).notice: Allows to check the amount of reward tokens earned by a perpetual

forceClosePerpetuals(uint256[]).notice: Allows an outside caller to close perpetuals if too much of the collateral from users is hedged by HAs

getApproved(uint256).notice: Gets the approved address by a perpetual owner

getCashOutAmount(uint256,uint256).notice: Returns the `cashOutAmount` of the perpetual owned by someone at a given oracle value

getReward(uint256).notice: Allows a perpetual owner to withdraw rewards

haBonusMalusDeposit().notice: Extra parameter from the `FeeManager` contract that is multiplied to the fees from above and that can be used to change deposit fees. It works as a bonus - malus fee, if `haBonusMalusDeposit > BASE_PARAMS`, then the fee will be larger than `haFeesDeposit`, if `haBonusMalusDeposit < BASE_PARAMS`, fees will be smaller. This parameter, updated by keepers in the `FeeManager` contract, could most likely depend on the collateral ratio

haBonusMalusWithdraw().notice: Extra parameter from the `FeeManager` contract that is multiplied to the fees from above and that can be used to change withdraw fees. It works as a bonus - malus fee, if `haBonusMalusWithdraw > BASE_PARAMS`, then the fee will be larger than `haFeesWithdraw`, if `haBonusMalusWithdraw < BASE_PARAMS`, fees will be smaller

isApprovedForAll(address,address).notice: Gets if the operator address is approved on all perpetuals by the owner

isApprovedOrOwner(address,uint256).notice: Gets if the sender address is approved for the perpetualId

keeperFeesClosingCap().notice: Cap on the fees that go to keepers closing perpetuals when too much collateral is hedged by HAs (hedge ratio above `limitHAHedge`) If a keeper forces the closing of n perpetuals in a single transaction, then this keeper is entitled to get as much as `keeperFeesClosingCap`. This cap amount is independent of the number of perpetuals closed

keeperFeesLiquidationCap().notice: Cap on the fees that go to keepers liquidating a perpetual If a keeper liquidates n perpetuals in a single transaction, then this keeper is entitled to get as much as `n * keeperFeesLiquidationCap` as a reward

keeperFeesLiquidationRatio().notice: Portion of the leftover cash out amount of liquidated perpetuals that go to liquidating keepers

limitHAHedge().notice: Limit proportion of stablecoins issued using this collateral that HAs can insure Above this ratio `forceCashOut` is activated and anyone can see its perpetual cashed out

liquidatePerpetuals(uint256[]).notice: Allows an outside caller to liquidate perpetuals if their margin ratio is under the maintenance margin

lockTime().notice: Amount of time before HAs are allowed to withdraw funds from their perpetuals either using `removeFromPerpetual` or `closePerpetual`. New perpetuals cannot be forced closed in situations where the `forceClosePerpetuals` function is activated before this `lockTime` elapsed

maintenanceMargin().notice: Maintenance Margin (in `BASE_PARAMS`) for each perpetual The margin ratio is defined for a perpetual as: `(initMargin + PnL) / committedAmount` where `PnL = committedAmount * (1 - initRate/currentRate)` If the `marginRatio` is below `maintenanceMargin`: then the perpetual can be liquidated

maxLeverage().notice: Maximum leverage multiplier authorized for HAs (`in BASE_PARAMS`) Leverage for a perpetual here corresponds to the ratio between the amount committed and the margin of the perpetual

name().notice: Gets the name of the NFT collection implemented by this contract

notifyRewardAmount(uint256).notice: Notifies the contract that rewards are going to be shared among HAs of this pool

openPerpetual(address,uint256,uint256,ui.notice: Lets a HA join the protocol and create a perpetual

oracle().notice: `Oracle` to give the rate feed, that is the price of the collateral with respect to the price of the stablecoin This reference can be modified by the corresponding `StableMaster` contract

ownerOf(uint256).notice: Gets the owner of the perpetual with ID perpetualID

pause().notice: Pauses the `getReward` method as well as the functions allowing to open, modify or close perpetuals

periodFinish().notice: Below are parameters that can also be found in other staking contracts to be able to compute rewards from staking (having perpetuals here) correctly

perpetualRewardPerTokenPaid(uint256).notice: Mapping used to compute the rewards earned by a perpetual in a timeframe

recoverERC20(address,address,uint256).notice: Supports recovering LP Rewards from other systems such as BAL to be distributed to holders or tokens that were mistakenly

removeFromPerpetual(uint256,uint256,addr.notice: Lets a HA decrease the `margin` in a perpetual she controls for this stablecoin/collateral pair

rewardToken().notice: Interface for the `rewardToken` distributed as a reward As of Angle V1, only a single `rewardToken` can be distributed to HAs who own a perpetual This implementation assumes that reward tokens have a base of 18 decimals

rewards(uint256).notice: Mapping used to get how much rewards in governance tokens are gained by a perpetual

safeTransferFrom(address,address,uint256.notice: Safely transfers the `perpetualID` from an address to another without data in it
Safely transfers the `perpetualID` from an address to another with data in the transfer

setApprovalForAll(address,bool).notice: Sets approval on all perpetuals owned by the owner to an operator

setBaseURI(string).notice: Sets `baseURI` that is the URI to access ERC721 metadata

setBoundsPerpetual(uint64,uint64).notice: Changes the maximum leverage authorized (commit/margin) and the maintenance margin under which perpetuals can be liquidated

setFeeKeeper(uint64,uint64).notice: Updates all the fees not depending on individual HA conditions via keeper utils functions

setFeeManager(address).notice: Changes the reference to the `FeeManager` contract

setHAFees(uint64[],uint64[],uint8).notice: Sets `xHAFees` that is the thresholds of values of the ratio between what's covered (hedged) divided by what's to hedge with HAs at which fees will change as well as `yHAFees` that is the value of the deposit or withdraw fees at threshold

setKeeperFeesCap(uint256,uint256).notice: Sets the maximum amounts going to the keepers when closing perpetuals because too much was hedged by HAs or when liquidating a perpetual

setKeeperFeesClosing(uint64[],uint64[]).notice: Sets the x-array (ie thresholds) for `FeeManager` when closing perpetuals and the y-array that is the value of the proportions of the fees going to keepers closing perpetuals

setKeeperFeesLiquidationRatio(uint64).notice: Sets the portion of the leftover cash out amount of liquidated perpetuals that go to keepers

setLockTime(uint64).notice: Sets `lockTime` that is the minimum amount of time HAs have to stay within the protocol

setNewRewardsDistribution(address).notice: Changes the `rewardsDistribution` associated to this contract

setOracle(address).notice: Changes the oracle contract used to compute collateral price with respect to the stablecoin's price

setRewardDistribution(uint256,address).notice: Sets the conditions and specifies the duration of the reward distribution

setTargetAndLimitHAHedge(uint64,uint64).notice: Sets the target and limit proportions of collateral from users that can be insured by HAs

supportsInterface(bytes4).notice: Queries if a contract implements an interface

symbol().notice: Gets the symbol of the NFT collection implemented by this contract

targetHAHedge().notice: Target proportion of stablecoins issued using this collateral to insure with HAs. This variable is exactly the same as the one in the `StableMaster` contract for this collateral. Above this hedge ratio, HAs cannot open new perpetuals When keepers are forcing the closing of some perpetuals, they are incentivized to bringing the hedge ratio to this proportion

totalHedgeAmount().notice: Total amount of stablecoins that are insured (i.e. that could be redeemed against collateral thanks to HAs) When a HA opens a perpetual, it covers/hedges a fixed amount of stablecoins for the protocol, equal to the committed amount times the entry rate `totalHedgeAmount` is the sum of all these hedged amounts

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).notice: Transfers the `perpetualID` from an address to another

xHAFeesDeposit(uint256).notice: Deposit fees for HAs depend on the hedge ratio that is the ratio between what is hedged (or covered, this is a synonym) by HAs compared with the total amount to hedgeThresholds for the ratio between to amount hedged and the amount to hedge The bigger the ratio the bigger the fees will be because this means that the max amount to insure is soon to be reached

xHAFeesWithdraw(uint256).notice: Withdraw fees for HAs also depend on the hedge ratioThresholds for the hedge ratio

xKeeperFeesClosing(uint256).notice: Thresholds on the values of the rate between the current hedged amount (`totalHedgeAmount`) and the target hedged amount by HAs (`targetHedgeAmount`) divided by 2. A value of `0.5` corresponds to a hedge ratio of `1`. Doing this allows to maintain an array with values of `x` inferior to `BASE_PARAMS`.

yHAFeesDeposit(uint256).notice: Deposit fees at threshold values This array should have the same length as the array above The evolution of the fees between two threshold values is linear

yKeeperFeesClosing(uint256).notice: Values at thresholds of the proportions of the fees that should go to keepers closing perpetuals

userdoc.notice: `PerpetualManager` is the contract handling all the Hedging Agents perpetuals
